title: Russian Attack Kills at Least Six in Ukraine, Cuts Power to Over 500,000, Days After 'Energy Ceasefire'
excerpt: Russia's defence ministry said it carried out a 'massive' strike on energy and communications infrastructure. President Zelenskyy said Ukraine received no early warning of the ballistic missile attack from its Western partners.
body:
• Russian air attacks killed at least six people across Ukraine and left more than 500,000 people without power, according to Al Jazeera reporting from Kyiv.
  • Russia's defence ministry said its forces carried out a "massive" strike on communications and energy infrastructure, including two power and heating plants in Kyiv.
  • President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of violating the "energy ceasefire" announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday, and said partners gave no early warning of the attack.
  • Ukraine reported downing large numbers of drones over Russia in return strikes; Moscow said 902 Ukrainian drones were shot down overnight.

Russian air attacks have killed at least six people in Ukraine and left hundreds of thousands without power, days after US President Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" in the more than four-year war, Al Jazeera reported. The Russian Defence Ministry said on Wednesday that its forces had carried out a "massive" strike against communications and energy infrastructure facilities in Ukraine, the Interfax news agency reported.

According to the ministry, Russian forces hit two plants supplying power and heating in Kyiv, two other plants in the wider region and an electricity substation, as well as a heating and power plant in Kharkiv, a thermal facility it said supplied the Ukrainian military in the southeast of the Kharkiv region, and a data centre in Kyiv it said was used to gather intelligence on Russia's military.

Deaths and blackouts in the capital

Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko urged people to remain in shelters, writing on Telegram that energy facilities in Kyiv and the surrounding region had come under a massive ballistic missile strike and that there were power disruptions in the capital. DTEK, Ukraine's largest private energy provider, said the attack caused emergency power cuts in several urban districts of Kyiv.

A Russian strike on a multistorey building in the capital's Desnianskyi district killed two people, and another attack in the Golosiivsky district killed one, Ukraine's state emergency service said. The Ukrainian military reported two people killed and six wounded in the Dnipropetrovsk region, and another person killed in the Zaporizhzhia region. Further missile attacks were reported in the Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions, with other strikes hitting Sumy and Chernihiv.

Al Jazeera's Audrey MacAlpine, reporting from Kyiv, said a record number of hypersonic missiles were used in the attacks on the capital, and that over half a million people in Ukraine were without power as a result of the strikes.

Zelenskyy: no warning, and a ceasefire broken

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine received no warnings from its Western partners of the Russian ballistic missile attack, raising questions about intelligence sharing. He wrote on Facebook that Ukraine detected the missiles only as they neared Kyiv.

"A targeted Russian ballistic missile strike specifically against energy infrastructure – the very infrastructure covered by the ceasefire announced by the American President."

— Volodymyr Zelenskyy, President of Ukraine

A technology adviser to the Ukrainian president also said the operation of some Starlink terminals appeared to have been restricted overnight, with a speed limit applied to terminals in motion that disrupted combat missions. The adviser said Ukraine's defence forces were not warned about the restriction.

Ukraine strikes back

Russia also reported Ukrainian drone strikes overnight. The governor of Russia's Saratov region, Roman Busargin, said a Ukrainian drone strike killed one person in the city of Balakovo. Sberbank later said its data centre in the Saratov region was attacked by drones but that all systems were operating as normal. Moscow mayor Sergey Sobyanin said air defence forces downed nearly 500 drones flying towards the Russian capital, and Russia's military later put the total number of downed Ukrainian drones at 902, of which 180 were shot down near Moscow.

What to watch

The attack, coming within days of the energy ceasefire announcement, puts the credibility of that arrangement — and of US intelligence support to Kyiv — at the centre of the next round of diplomacy. Power restoration timelines from DTEK and any US response to Zelenskyy's ceasefire charge are the immediate signals to watch.
